div.head: Af El. 49.6
div.ab: I. On ðyssum anum dome mon mæg geþencan, ðæt he æghwylcne (dom) on ryht gedeme; ne þearf he nanre domboca oþera (cépan). Geðænce he, ðæt he nanum men ne deme þæt he nolde ðæt man him demde, gif he þone dom ofer hine ahte.

I. Of ðissum anum dome mon mæg geðencean, þæt he æghwelcne on ryht gedemeð; ne ðearf he nanra domboca oþerra. Geðence he, þæt he nanum men ne deme þæt he nolde ðæt he him demde, gif he ðone dóm ofer hine sohte.

Ex hoc uno iudicio perpendi potest, ut unicuique iustum iudicetur; nec opus est aliquo libro iudiciali preter hoc fatigari, quam ne quis alii iudicet quod sibi iudicari nollet, si iudicium haberetur super eum.

{I} Of ðissum anum dome mon mæg geðencean, þæt he æghwelcne on ryht gedemeð; ne ðearf he nanra domboca oþerra. Geðence he, þæt he nanum men ne deme þæt he nolde ðæt he him demde, gif he ðone dóm ofer hine sohte.

From this one judgment one may reason in such a way that he judge each man rightly; he requires no other book of laws. Let him think that he judge no man in a manner that he would not be judged by him, if he sought judgment over him.

Aus dieser Einen Satzung kann der Mensch eingedenk sein, dass er jeden nach Recht beurtheilt; und [dann] bedarf er keiner anderen Gesetzbücher. Sei er eingedenk, dass er keinem Menschen zuerkenne, was er nicht wollen würde, dass dieser ihm zuerkennte, wenn er das Urtheil über sich [unter diesem Urtheilfinder] nachsuchte.

From this one precept a person can bear in mind that he judges everyone according to right; and [then] he needs no other law-books. Let him bear in mind that he should adjudge to no person what he would not wish that person to adjudge to him, if he sought judgment upon himself [from that judge].
div.note: From here on Liebermann’s second text column is H; G ends at El. 49.5.
